text:
lena: FYI noticed a cluster health blip in eu-west1 this morning. Lots of GPU slots reported free but job failures climbed. Looks like network egress is the common factor.
arjun: Can you share the alert? which nodes?
lena: ops alert 9234 and 9235 -> node.egress.percent > 85% on several racks. Example dump:
```
$ kubectl describe node eu-west1-node-17 | egrep 'Allocated resources|Non-terminated Pods:|Annotations:' -A2
Non-terminated Pods:         (34 in total)
  Namespace                  Name                     CPU Requests  CPU Limits  Memory Requests  Memory Limits  GPU
  default                    stream-preproc-7         500m          -           1Gi              -              0
  ml                         training-large-01        8000m         -           32Gi             -              2
Allocated resources:  16 CPUs, 64Gi memory, 2 GPUs
Annotations: egress_mbps=680
```
node has 2 GPUs allocated/available but egress at 680 Mbps (we usually consider >600 a "hot egress" for mixed racks).
tessa: So scheduler placed the large training job because GPUs looked available, but the NIC became a bottleneck -> packets retried -> driver logs show NVLink retries -> small pods OOM/killed -> kubelet evictions cascade.
arjun: This is the classic "ghost-GPU": resource appears free but adjacent resource (egress) is saturated so the workload misbehaves.
lena: Immediate action I ran: cordon + drain non-gang streaming pods on top 3 noisy nodes and moved them to dedicated network-heavy warmpool. Commands I used:
```
kubectl cordon eu-west1-node-17
kubectl drain eu-west1-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='job-type!=gang' --force
```
That dropped node egress by ~40% within 3 minutes.
ops-bot: runbook hint: /runbooks/egress-vs-gpu -> step 1: cordon noisy nodes; step 2: isolate high-egress services; step 3: consider node tainting.
tessa: Short-term mitigation proposals:
- Add a node taint/key when node.egress_mbps > 600 (taint: egress-hot=true:NoSchedule)
- Prefer scheduling multi-gang GPU pods onto nodes with egress_mbps < 400 via a scheduler scoring plugin
- Add a QoS class or cgroup limit for tenant egress on mixed racks
arjun: I can prototype a lightweight scoring plugin: subtract penalty proportional to egress_mbps/1000 from score for gpu-gang pods. Feature-flagged rollout only.
lena: Rollout plan:
- Alpha in eu-west1: label 10% of nodes as canary=true, plugin enabled for pods with label workload=gang-train
- Metrics: eviction_rate (per-node), job_retries (per-workload), tail_latency for inference services (to detect regressions)
- Success gate: eviction_rate <= baseline * 1.3 and job_retries <= 3%
arjun: We'll also add telemetry: expose rack.egress_capacity label (low/med/high) from infra inventory so scheduler can avoid hot racks.
tessa: For immediate automation I can wire a k8s cron to apply taint when Prometheus node exporter reports egress_mbps > 650 for 2 minutes. Will post PR with tests.
lena: Cost note: during the 6h window, we saw ~22% more preempted GPU-hours and a ~12% increase in job-runtime due to retries. Need to tag cost impact on the incident.
runbook-bot: Creating incident ticket inc-20260305-egress-gpu. Suggested next step: perf profile of scoring plugin on canary nodes.
arjun: I'll open the KEP + PR and add perf hooks (histogram of scheduling decisions, time-to-start for gang pods, observed egress at placement).
tessa: I'll own the tainting cron and the emergency cordon script (will add --dry-run tests).
lena: Great. Follow-ups: add rack-egress label item to infra backlog, measure multi-tenant egress patterns to tune thresholds, and roll canary to ap-southeast if stable.
arjun: One more gotcha: avoid tight coupling of egress metric to scheduling for latency-sensitive inference pods; these need a different policy. We'll gate by pod annotation scheduling-hint=egress-aware.
lena: TL;DR: network hotness + naive GPU packing = apparent free GPUs but high eviction/retry. Short-term: cordon/taint noisy nodes + QoS. Medium-term: scheduler scoring plugin + rack egress labels + telemetry. Thanks all :party_parrot:
